lyric_resham.en: Traditional folk song every Nepali kid grows up hearing. 'Resham' means silk, 'firiri' is the fluttering motion — like silk dancing in the wind. Playful, upbeat, about beauty and joy. Composed by Buddhi Pariyar, collected from Pokhara villages. First recorded at Radio Nepal in 1969, sung by Sunder Shrestha and Dwarika Lal Joshi.

lyric_jechhau.en: Swoopna Suman × Samir Shrestha (2023). 'However you are.' Key line — 'Je chhau jaso chhau timi, tehi nai ho malai chahine' — 'no matter who you are, you're the one I need.' About loving someone exactly as they are.

lyric_exmaros.en: Jhapalish (2025, hip-hop). 'May my ex die' — playful, not serious. 'Maros' is slang for 'die,' used jokingly. A diss track for when you're over someone.

lyric_deuralima.en: Prem Dhoj Pradhan (classic, music by Natikaji). 'The wind blew at Deurali' — Deurali is a mountain pass where travelers rest. Nostalgic, about wind carrying memories through the hills. Makes Nepalis abroad homesick.

lyric_sastomutu.en: Sajjan Raj Vaidya. 'Cheap heart' — 'sasto' means cheap, 'mutu' means heart. About feeling like your love wasn't valued. Sad but beautiful.

lyric_kutumakutu.en: Rajan Raj Shiwakoti & Melina Rai (2017, from Dui Rupaiyan). 243M views — the most-watched Nepali video ever. 'Kutu ma kutu' is the sound of chewing something hard; 'supari dana' is areca nut. Offering supari is how you invite someone to a function in Nepali culture — they chew it to accept. Pure celebration.

lyric_rukummaikot.en: SD Yogi & Shanti Shree Pariyar (2024, from Khusma). 193M views — fastest Nepali song to 100M. Rukum is a district in western Nepal, Maikot is a village there. A folk-pop love letter to the region.
